Method of Attack: Use of malicious Microsoft Word document with embedded macro
Macro protected with password and base64 encoding
Malware binary packed with Enigma Protector for evasion
Use of fake host header in HTTP POST requests to C2 servers
Data collection, encryption, and exfiltration over HTTP
Execution of commands on infected machine
Discoverer: IBM X-Force Incident Response and Intelligence Services (IRIS)
Qi An Xin cyber security company
Impacted Systems: Microsoft Windows systems (implied by use of .exe binaries and Microsoft Word documents)
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious Word documents
Malicious Word template downloaded from Google Drive
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious Word document in Arabic prompting to enable editing
Google Drive links hosting malicious Word templates and backdoor binaries
Backdoor binaries packed with Enigma Protector and Themida
Fake host headers in HTTP POST requests: 'cnet].[com' (spoofed), real hosts 'nysura].[com' and 'webtutorialz[.]com'
Command and control domains (at least 15 identified)
Files: runawy.exe, blaster.exe, Wordeditor.exe, soundcloud.exe, HelpPane.exe, taskmanager.exe
Date of Discovery: October 31 and November 2, 2019 (Palo Alto Networks report)
